messages:
Alex M: Kicking off onboarding for 'banyan-embed-xxl' — baseline vs quantized int6/int4 on the anchor+wiki holdout. Quick smoke, will post numbers as they finish.
Sara P: Nice. Which evaluation slices are you running? short queries / multi-sentence?
Alex M: anchor_wiki (mix), short_queries, cluster_sample (50k). Also hierarchical clustering + silhouette and recall@1/5/10.
Mike L: Please run cosine and dot-product variants, we've seen ranking flip for scaled vectors.
Alex M: good call. Doing both.
Alex M: Running the harness now:
```
./run_eval --model banyan-embed-xxl --quant int6 --slices anchor_wiki,short_queries,cluster_sample 
  --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,silhouette,mean_cosine 
  --sim_metric cosine,dot --topk 10 --pca_whiten true
```
Reena D: FYI add a seed=42 and report variance across 3 seeds if time permits. Small instabilities matter for canary.
Alex M: Will do. First pass (single seed) results are in:
```
Model            quant   slice           recall@1  recall@5  recall@10  silhouette  mean_cosine
banyan-embed-xxl  fp32    anchor_wiki     0.672     0.842     0.903      0.21        0.124
banyan-embed-xxl  int6    anchor_wiki     0.657     0.829     0.891      0.19        0.119
banyan-embed-xxl  int4    anchor_wiki     0.601     0.780     0.848      0.16        0.105
```
Sara P: int6 looks within tolerance for anchor_wiki but int4 is getting shaky. What's short_queries?
Alex M: short_queries slice:
```
fp32 recall@1 0.418  recall@5 0.610  recall@10 0.682  silhouette 0.09
int6 recall@1 0.365  recall@5 0.582  recall@10 0.645  silhouette 0.07
int4 recall@1 0.287  recall@5 0.490  recall@10 0.553  silhouette 0.04
```
Mike L: Oof short queries are sensitive. Could be quantization noise for very short context vectors. Did you try per-channel quant (per-channel asymmetric) vs global?
Alex M: This run used per-tensor. I'll run per-channel next.
Alex M: Also saw cluster_sample silhouette dropped from 0.21 -> 0.12 (fp32 -> int6). Visual check on UMAP shows more banding.
Reena D: Can you compute nearest-neighbor id-flip rate for k=1 across fp32 vs int6? That's a useful signal.
Alex M: Yes. id-flip (fraction of anchors whose top-1 neighbor changed): fp32 vs int6 = 0.034, fp32 vs int4 = 0.127.
Sara P: 3.4% flip for int6 is acceptable for some customers but depends on downstream. We should mark as "canary" not full rollout.
Mike L: For short_queries, maybe try small-dim PCA + whitening before quant to stabilize magnitude differences.
Alex M: Ran per-channel int6 + PCA(256) whitening:
```
perchannel-int6 + pca256 anchor_wiki recall@1 0.662 recall@5 0.835 silhouette 0.195
perchannel-int6 + pca256 short_queries recall@1 0.401 recall@5 0.598 silhouette 0.085
id-flip vs fp32 = 0.021
```
Sara P: That reduces flips to 2.1% — much better. short_queries still slightly down but closer.
Reena D: Please post the 3-seed averages before we decide. Also add a few real-customer queries if available (redact).
eval-bot: Scheduled job started: eval-3935001234-3seeds (banyan-embed-xxl, perchannel-int6, pca256). ETA ~18m.
Alex M: Putting provisional recommendation: per-channel int6 + PCA whitening as "canary" with rollout 5% traffic to start, monitor recall@1 and id-flip, and enable fallback to fp32 on regressions > 2.5% for critical routes.
Mike L: Agreed. Also track latency and memory — int6 reduced exec mem by ~28% in local run, but check tail latency.
Alex M: Local perf: p99 latency steady, 6% faster token throughput. Will run perf bench on dedicated infra next.
Sara P: Thanks — good work. Tagging @infra-oncall for perf bench and @solutions for customer-impact review. :thumbsup:
Reena D: One more: add silhouette per-cluster percent drop (we care if specific clusters collapse).
Alex M: Will attach cluster-level diffs once 3-seed run completes.
